question: Which funding proposal in this corpus requested the largest amount of GCF funding?

expect.notes: H3 corpus-wide extremum, MAX arm. DERIVATION: over all 273 registry rows, take registry.canonical(doc,'gcf_funding_requested'); keep candidates with currency=='USD' AND value is not None (the parse guard that rejects a print whose mantissa and scale word contradict each other). 172 of 273 rows qualify. The maximum is FP241 'Financing Mitigation and Adaptation Projects (FMAP) in Indian MSMEs' (Small Industries Development Bank of India, B.39 2024), raw '2149 million USD' = 2,149,000,000 USD, p.5 section A.8. Double-attested: registry.json v1 carries the same string, and the VLM extraction data/extracted/vlm/qwen_qwen2.5-vl-7b/35_gcf-b39-02-add16-rev01-funding-proposal-package-fp241.md prints '## A.8 Total GCF funding requested' / '2149 million USD (multi-country proposals: clause 19 on annex 17)'. ROBUSTNESS CHECK: FP241 is the maximum under all three defensible inclusion rules - USD any section, USD template-A.8 only, and any-currency-including-unstamped - so this expectation does not depend on which guard the concurrent extremum mechanism implements. Runner-up is FP25 at 382.5 million USD, so the winner is not close. ROWS EXCLUDED, and why: the 19 rows whose canonical value is None because the printed unit is self-contradictory - FP162 '82,849 million USD', FP53 '31,385 million USD', FP18 '$37,460 million USD', FP199 '$36,232 million USD', FP45 '34,357 | million USD', FP153 '28,654 million USD', FP68 '27 054 | million USD', FP11 '$20,546,756 million USD', FP51 'US$ 17,346 million', FP23 '9,500,000 | million USD', FP75 '$5,000,000 million USD', FP3 '7,614,280 | million USD', FP270 '50 USD', FP168 '175.9 USD', FP115 'US$ 60.0', FP114 'US$12.95', plus EUR-side FP262, FP103, FP89. Read literally, six of those would outrank FP241 (FP162 alone would read as 82.8 billion), which is exactly the trap this case exists to catch - the mechanism must exclude them, and so does this expectation. Also excluded: 21 rows priced in EUR (largest FP117, 304 million EUR - not comparable without an FX rate the corpus does not carry) and 61 rows with no gcf_funding_requested candidate at all. Denominator for an honest answer: 172 of 273 rows state a comparable USD figure. No must_not_contain: a correct answer may legitimately quote an excluded ambiguous print while explaining why it was excluded, so any forbid on those numerals would punish the honest answer. docs [] - corpus-level, answerable only from a computed note; requiring retrieval to surface FP241's package from a question that never names it would measure the wrong thing.

question: How many countries does FP151 cover? List them.

expect.notes: F13/P5, the silent-truncation falsehood the deterministic verifier certified: the note used to print ', '.join(countries[:5]) with no count, the system answered 'five', and the claim scored SUPPORTED. DERIVATION: registry.by_fp(151)['countries'] has len 44; the first five, which are the five the note prints, are Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi. Confirmed today that registry_note('How many countries does FP151 cover? List them.') emits 'countries (5 of 44 - list truncated): Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, ... (p.3)'. MUST_CONTAIN picks 44 plus two names from those printed five - an answer cannot be asked to name country 6..44, which the note does not carry, so the expectation stays inside what the evidence can support. MUST_NOT_CONTAIN forbids the AFFIRMATIVE five-is-the-total claim only. Tested against both phrasings, as required: 'FP151 covers five countries.' MATCHES (forbidden), 'FP151 covers 5 countries: Angola, Benin, ...' MATCHES (forbidden); the honest forms do NOT match - 'FP151 covers 44 countries; the registry note lists 5 of 44', 'the note names 5 countries out of the 44', 'only 5 of the 44 are shown', 'It covers 44 countries. Five are listed here: Angola, ...'. Two devices do that work: the verb list contains only verbs that assert the PROPOSAL's coverage (covers/spans/comprises/includes/targets/is implemented in) and not the verbs that describe the NOTE's listing (lists/names/shows), and the negative lookahead cancels the match when 44 appears within the same sentence. pages [] even though the countries array is a cover-page fact (A.1.3, p.3): a retrieval-only run of this exact question puts the FP151 package at rank 1 but never surfaces p.3 in the top 10, and the fact is answered from the registry note rather than from a retrieved page - which is why id-fp151-entity and id-fp234-entity also leave pages empty for cover-page facts. Claiming p.3 here would book a 0% evidence-page hit against a case the system answers correctly.

This case pins the value a computed total must produce. ARITHMETIC, from registry.canonical(doc,'gcf_funding_requested') over the 30 rows registry.by_year(2020) returns with an fp, keeping only candidates with currency=='USD' and a non-None parsed value: FP124 39,780,000 + FP126 38,266,790.80 + FP128 25,000,000 + FP129 17,198,843 + FP131 27,600,000 + FP133 32,700,000 + FP135 38,000,000 + FP136 165,237,562 + FP137 30,100,000 + FP140 180,890,000 + FP141 23,101,276 + FP143 99,500,000 + FP145 29,837,169 + FP146 64,094,029 + FP147 47,403,174 + FP148 30,000,000 + FP149 100,000,000 + FP151 18,500,000 + FP152 150,000,000 = 1,157,208,843.80 USD over 19 of the 30 rows. EXCLUSIONS, and why: FP132 (32.79 million Eur) and FP138 (55,415,176 Eur) are a different currency and the corpus carries no FX rate; FP153 ('28,654 million USD') parses to value None because the mantissa and the scale word cannot both be true - it is the single print that made the hallucinated total 21x too high; FP125, FP127, FP130, FP134, FP139, FP144 state no GCF figure anywhere; FP142 ('$82,000,000') and FP150 ('256.48 million USD') have a v1 string but NO v2 canonical candidate, so they carry no verified parse and are out of the same-basis sum. If the concurrent implementation chooses to fold those two v1-only rows in, the total becomes 1,495,688,843.80 over 21 rows and this case's first regex fails loudly rather than silently - that is the intended signal, and the fork is recorded here so the coordinator can retune one regex instead of re-deriving. The \b19\b check is the denominator claim: an honest total says how many of the 30 rows it covers. MUST_NOT_CONTAIN forbids any two-or-more-digit billions figure - '29 billion', '$85 billion' - while leaving '1.157 billion' and '1.16 billion' free, because the lookbehind refuses a number that follows a decimal point. Regex tolerates the three magnitude formats a correct answer might print: 1,157,208,843(.80), 1,157.2 million, 1.157/1.16 billion. docs [] - corpus-level.
